reasons: Classification is defensible: the existing Section 14 meets workers' comp, CGL, E&O 1M and certificate elements but contains no cyber/privacy cover, and the playbook fallback expressly requires cyber of at least USD 2M — so the clause fails the fallback on a material term rather than a minor sub-element.

The redline is a targeted insertion of 'cyber liability (including privacy and data breach) insurance with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000)' into the existing coverage list, leaving all other clause mechanics intact; this is the smallest edit that reaches the fallback position.

The advisory changed-character ratio (0.633) overstates the intervention — the rendered redline shows only an added phrase within the same sentence structure, so the minimal-edit concern is not substantiated.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix; it states what was added, cites the preferred USD 5M position and explains acceptance of the USD 2M fallback given the consulting scope, without lecturing.
Directionally correct for the Customer: the edit adds protection without expanding our obligations, and the finding does not duplicate another rule's commercial term.
